The new transparency obligations under the bloc’s landmark AI Act came into effect on August 2nd, requiring companies to disclose when people are interacting with AI models, and if content has been generated or altered by them.
The transparency rules differ between providers (companies that develop and market AI systems) and deployers (platforms and services that use those AI systems), though some companies like Meta and SpaceXAI are classified as both.

Providers must design AI systems to explicitly notify users when they’re dealing with AI instead of a human, “unless this is obvious,” and include machine-readable marks on synthetic audio, image, video, and text so that it can be detected as artificially generated or manipulated. The Commission has also developed a set of AI disclosure labels that tech platforms can adopt in accordance with the AI Act rules, alongside examples of when they should be used. These mirror similar labels that have already been introduced by TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook. articles.title: After killer quarter, Palantir CEO Alex Karp calls AI industry ‘Marxist’
articles.summary: After a quarter that delivered $1 billion in profit, Palantir CEO Alex Karp on Monday once again warned that AI frontier labs are too untrustworthy for enterprises.
articles.full_body:
Title: After killer quarter, Palantir CEO Alex Karp calls AI industry ‘Marxist’

URL Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/03/after-killer-quarter-palantir-ceo-alex-karp-calls-ai-industry-marxist

Published Time: 2026-08-03T23:19:50+00:00

Markdown Content:
Palantir CEO Alex Karp on Monday once again warned that AI frontier labs are too untrustworthy for enterprises.

The CEO, who famously studied philosophy and earned a PhD in social theory, implied in Palantir’s quarterly shareholder letter that these were the kinds of capitalists who gave rise to Marxist socialism.

“There are Marxist overtones and undertones to our business,” he wrote in a letter to [shareholders about Palantir’s outstanding quarter he wrote](https://www.palantir.com/q2-2026-letter/en/). “Others, including many of those building large language models, intend, knowingly or otherwise, to capture the means of production of their purported partners.”

To be clear, AI labs have hardly cornered Palantir out of the market. Quite the opposite. The skyrocketing use of AI helped Palantir achieve record-breaking results. For its second quarter, the company [reported](https://investors.palantir.com/news-details/2026/Palantir-Reports-Q2-2026-U-S--Comm-Revenue-Growth-of-149-YY-and-Revenue-Growth-of-93-YY-Raises-FY-2026-Revenue-Guidance-to-82-YY-Growth-and-U-S--Comm-Revenue-Guidance-to-134-YY-Crushing-Consensus-Expectations/) $1.9 billion in revenue, up 93% over the year-ago quarter, and $1.1 billion in profit, “more profit in a single quarter than we did in total revenue in the same period the year before,” he wrote.

During the quarterly conference call with Wall Street analysts, he explained his analogy further, relying heavily on a sort of “tech bro patriot” jargon common among defense tech companies. (Palantir’s senior leadership is entirely male.)

He asked on the call, if companies are going “to buy into a future” where your job helps your “adversaries win, and everybody who does win is a small, tiny group of people living in a tiny place that somehow believe because they eat vegetables and they don’t support war fighters that they deserve to have the total means of production of this country? And the rest of us should just sit by it back and absorb the cost of that revolution, which we’re paying for.”

Palantir, in contrast, serves model-agnostic AI and analysis software to governments and enterprises, and allows organizations to control their data as well as their AI “exhaust,” aka, their prompts, orchestration, context.

“How are we paying for it? In the enterprise context, people sign up for token self pleasurings… at real cost like other forms of self pleasure,” he said. “You are paying for the right for them to migrate your IP, your know-how, your expertise to their model, so that they can build a competitive business that doesn’t require your business or people. And why are they doing it? It’s actually being done for what they believe are moral reasons. They are superior to you. They deserve to colonize your enterprise.”

Jarring language aside, he is making an underlying point that is increasingly being repeated elsewhere, including from the likes of [Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/29/microsoft-is-openly-competing-with-openai-anthropic-more-than-ever/)

This theory points to the [significant list of companies](https://x.com/itsolelehmann/status/2082644674981089564) that partnered or paid for Anthropic and OpenAI while the AI labs launched similar businesses ranging from design tools to, healthcare operations, legal, even drug discovery.

The truth is, none of these companies are economic villains or heroes — anymore than other for-profit companies are. AI is growing so quickly, the market changing so rapidly, there is clearly room for all, Palantir’s results show.

The release had been expected after the company previewed the model last month, when it claimed it was “second only to Fable 5,” Anthropic’s flagship.
The open release of another highly capable Chinese AI model adds to sky-high tensions along multiple fronts in Silicon Valley and Washington over how to safely manage AI systems and retain the US’ technological edge over China. 
Results from Alibaba’s own testing shared on Monday suggests it’s as powerful as claimed, as does its ranking on crowdsourced model-comparison platform Arena.AI. Alibaba’s own testing shows the model’s performance to broadly match — and sometimes exceed — that of Fable 5 on benchmark tests. On the Arena text model leaderboard, Qwen3.8-Max trails only Fable 5 and three models in Anthropic’s Opus family. Open-weight releases have become a growing point of differentiation for China’s AI industry, where they have become the norm. Moonshot released Kimi K3’s last week and many other top AI models are also open-weight. Beijing has championed the strategy as a means of growing China’s influence in global AI governance and encouraging widespread adoption of domestic tech champions. 
Alibaba’s release intensifies competition with China, whose firms appear to be rapidly narrowing the gap with US companies and have increased the tempo of releases in recent weeks. articles.title: Apple finally fixed Siri. So why does it feel anticlimactic?
articles.summary: Apple’s long-awaited AI overhaul finally makes Siri the assistant it was always supposed to be. Yet it arrives at a moment when simply being a capable AI assistant no longer feels revolutionary.
articles.full_body:
Title: Apple finally fixed Siri. So why does it feel anticlimactic?

URL Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/03/apple-finally-fixed-siri-so-why-does-it-feel-anticlimactic

Published Time: 2026-08-03T18:43:43+00:00

Markdown Content:
After [rounds](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/apple-to-pay-250m-to-settle-lawsuit-over-siris-delayed-ai-features/) of [delays](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/11/apples-siri-revamp-reportedly-delayed-again/), [Siri AI arrived](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/14/apple-opens-its-new-siri-ai-to-everyone-with-the-ios-27-public-beta/) in the consumer beta build of iOS 27, [launched](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/13/apple-seeds-ios-27-public-beta-1/) in July. The AI assistant now does what Apple promised: It understands your personal context, taps into broad world knowledge to answer your questions, and surfaces relevant information stored on your iPhone.

And yet, the arrival feels somewhat anticlimactic. Apple finally has a functional — actually, a fairly impressive — AI assistant, but it’s arrived past the time where such a launch feels novel and exciting.

If anything, the AI race has surged ahead in the months and years Apple has [dawdled](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/07/ai-powered-more-personalized-siri-is-delayed/) on AI. Today, AI tools are coding and building software, AI agents are completing multistep tasks, and AI is working alongside you, using your computer, reasoning, thinking, remembering, creating media, and more. Being a functional chatbot or AI helper isn’t the breakthrough that it once would have been.

That is not to say [Apple’s Siri AI](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/06/apple-introduces-siri-ai-a-profoundly-more-capable-and-personal-assistant/) isn’t valuable or useful. With Siri AI’s launch, Apple delivered on its promises and then some.

You can now have natural, back-and-forth conversations with Siri, which has settings that let you tweak the expressivity and pacing of its voice responses. You can also type to the assistant, if you choose, or use it via a dedicated app for the first time, referencing past conversations.

The assistant can understand your personal context, helping you find things like photos, emails, contacts, texts, or calendar appointments — even when you’re not quite sure what you’re looking for or where. For instance, you could ask it to pull up the last receipt you saved on your iPhone, without saying where it was stored or what the receipt was for, and Siri will find it for you.

You can also ask it about things you’ve saved only as a photo, like your driver’s license number from a pic of your license, or a QR code you screenshotted to reference later, as a reminder to visit someone’s website. You can launch websites and use apps via Siri, doing things like getting directions, playing music, editing a photo, drafting an email, playing your audiobooks, and much more.

Thankfully, Siri now consistently and accurately plays the song, podcast, or audiobook you request on your preferred app — a low bar to be sure, but one [where Siri stumbled before](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=35731825).

Siri can brainstorm with you, too. Among other things, it can help you refine ideas, learn about a new topic, or explore a recipe — like suggesting something you can make with your random ingredients in your fridge! You can ask when your favorite band is playing or when a particular event is, and Siri answers correctly, giving you the information you need, based on your location.

You can use Siri in the camera’s viewfinder to learn about things in the real world or to help you split a restaurant bill with your friends.

In short, it’s exactly what you always hoped Siri would be: a useful assistant that lets you use your iPhone easily, just by talking, and one that can answer questions of any sort instead of shuffling you off to the web.

These [improvements](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/09/wwdc-2026-everything-announced-on-siri-ai-os-27-apple-intelligence-and-more/) were made possible by [Apple’s partnership with Google](https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/12/googles-gemini-to-power-apples-ai-features-like-siri/) for the use of its Gemini AI models. Apple didn’t just slap its name on Gemini AI; it used Google’s technology to train and refine its own proprietary Apple Foundation Models. The result is AI models designed to run on Apple’s own silicon and on its private cloud compute infrastructure and actually work.

Yet, despite finally delivering a functional, helpful version of Siri, it feels almost like Apple fixed a long-standing bug — a forever-broken Siri — rather than doing something revolutionary here. This is how Siri was meant to work all along. The only marvel is that, after so many years of failing to perform tasks correctly, it actually works.

The general public who don’t run beta builds on their devices will gain access to the new Siri when Apple officially releases iOS 27, expected in September.

# Congress’ favorite AI tool? ChatGPT

OpenAI’s ChatGPT is Congress’ AI tool of choice so far in terms of money spent, according to a [report from CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/03/openai-chatgpt-anthropic-congress-house-ai-spending.html).

OpenAI received roughly 90% of all spending on AI tools by House offices, committees, and institutional accounts during the year ending in March 31, per House disbursement records. CNBC found that Congress spent around $100,580 across 798 transactions on ChatGPT, out of at least $113,740 in total AI spending. Anthropic’s Claude trailed in second place at $13,160 across 37 transactions.

Democratic offices accounted for $54,165 in AI purchases, three times the $15,782 spent by Republican offices.

The insights exclude any Congressional AI adoption from free accounts or AI bundled into broader software contracts.

Congressional staffers are using ChatGPT and other tools to write memos, summarize and analyze legislation, respond to constituents, prepare hearing materials, sort through policy research, and even draft social media posts.

Palantir CEO Alex Karp on Monday once again warned that AI frontier labs are too untrustworthy for enterprises.

The CEO, who famously studied philosophy and earned a PhD in social theory, implied in Palantir’s quarterly shareholder letter that these were the kinds of capitalists who gave rise to Marxist socialism.

“There are Marxist overtones and undertones to our business,” he wrote in a letter to [shareholders about Palantir’s outstanding quarter he wrote](https://www.palantir.com/q2-2026-letter/en/). “Others, including many of those building large language models, intend, knowingly or otherwise, to capture the means of production of their purported partners.”

To be clear, AI labs have hardly cornered Palantir out of the market. Quite the opposite. The skyrocketing use of AI helped Palantir achieve record-breaking results. During the quarterly conference call with Wall Street analysts, he explained his analogy further, relying heavily on a sort of “tech bro patriot” jargon common among defense tech companies. (Palantir’s senior leadership is entirely male.)

He asked on the call, if companies are going “to buy into a future” where your job helps your “adversaries win, and everybody who does win is a small, tiny group of people living in a tiny place that somehow believe because they eat vegetables and they don’t support war fighters that they deserve to have the total means of production of this country?

fact_packs.headline: Apple finally fixed Siri. So why does it feel anticlimactic?
facts: Title: Apple finally fixed Siri. So why does it feel anticlimactic?

After [rounds](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/apple-to-pay-250m-to-settle-lawsuit-over-siris-delayed-ai-features/) of [delays](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/11/apples-siri-revamp-reportedly-delayed-again/), [Siri AI arrived](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/14/apple-opens-its-new-siri-ai-to-everyone-with-the-ios-27-public-beta/) in the consumer beta build of iOS 27, [launched](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/13/apple-seeds-ios-27-public-beta-1/) in July. The AI assistant now does what Apple

And yet, the arrival feels somewhat anticlimactic. Apple finally has a functional — actually, a fairly impressive — AI assistant, but it’s arrived past the time where such a launch feels novel and exciting.

If anything, the AI race has surged ahead in the months and years Apple has [dawdled](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/07/ai-powered-more-personalized-siri-is-delayed/) on AI. Today, AI tools are coding and building software, AI agents are completing multistep tasks, and AI is working alongside you, using your computer, reasoning, thinking, remembering, creating media, and more. Being a functional chatbot or AI helper isn’t the breakthrough that it once would have been.

That is not to say [Apple’s Siri AI](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/06/apple-introduces-siri-ai-a-profoundly-more-capable-and-personal-assistant/) isn’t valuable or useful. With Siri AI’s launch, Apple delivered on its promises and then some.

You can now have natural, back-and-forth conversations with Siri, which has settings that let you tweak the expressivity and pacing of its voice responses. You can also type to the assistant, if you choose, or use it via a dedicated app for the first time, referencing past conversations.

The assistant can understand your personal context, helping you find things like photos, emails, contacts, texts, or calendar appointments — even when you’re not quite sure what you’re looking for or where. For instance, you could ask it to pull up the last receipt you saved on your iPhone, without saying where it was stored or what the receipt was for, and Siri will find it for you.

You can also ask it about things you’ve saved only as a photo, like your driver’s license number from a pic of your license, or a QR code you screenshotted to reference later, as a reminder to visit someone’s website. You can launch websites and use apps via Siri, doing things like getting directions, playing music, editing a photo, drafting an email, playing your audiobooks, and much more.

reading.title: AI 监管落地、巨头互怼、Siri 迟到：今天的 AI 世界发生了什么？
reading.lead: 今天，欧洲的 AI 透明度规则正式生效，Palantir 的 CEO 用“马克思主义”炮轰 AI 巨头，阿里发布新模型叫板美国，苹果的 Siri AI 终于上线却显得过时，而 ChatGPT 成了美国国会的“新宠”。这些看似独立的事件，其实都指向同一个趋势：AI 正在从技术竞赛转向规则与权力的博弈。

sections.title: 欧洲 AI 透明度规则生效：AI 内容要“亮明身份”了
sections.dek: 从今天起，欧盟的 AI 法案透明度条款正式实施，聊天机器人和深度伪造内容必须明确标识。
sections.body:
今天，欧盟的 AI 透明度规则正式生效。这意味着，在欧洲，任何 AI 生成的深度伪造内容或聊天机器人，都必须明确告知用户“这是 AI”。这项规定是欧盟 AI 法案的一部分，旨在让人们在网上更容易识别 AI 的痕迹。

这项规则的核心，是要求 AI 系统在与人交互时，必须让用户知道自己在和机器对话；对于深度伪造内容，则要标注“这是 AI 生成的”。这就像食品包装上的配料表，让消费者知道吃的是什么。

对于科技公司来说，这意味着需要调整产品设计，增加标识功能。比如，聊天机器人可能需要自动介绍自己的 AI 身份，视频平台可能需要为 AI 生成的内容打上水印。

对于普通人来说，这项规则的好处是，你在网上看到的信息，更容易分辨真假。但它的执行效果，还要看各国监管机构的落实力度。毕竟，规则是一回事，执行是另一回事。

从产业角度看，这项规则可能增加企业的合规成本，尤其是那些在欧洲市场运营的 AI 公司。它们需要开发新的技术来标识 AI 内容，比如数字水印、元数据标记等。这可能会催生一个新的合规科技市场。

同时，这项规则也可能影响 AI 的传播方式。例如，社交媒体平台可能需要更严格地审核 AI 生成的内容，以避免违规。这可能会改变内容分发的逻辑，让 AI 内容的传播受到更多限制。

对于普通用户来说，这项规则意味着你在浏览网页、观看视频时，会看到更多的“AI 生成”标签。这有助于你做出更明智的判断，但也可能让你对 AI 内容产生更多警惕。

总的来说，欧洲的 AI 透明度规则是全球首个全面约束 AI 标识的法规，它可能成为其他国家的参考模板。对于科技公司来说，适应这些规则是进入欧洲市场的必要条件。对于普通人来说，这可能是 AI 监管时代的一个开端。

sections.title: Palantir CEO 炮轰 AI 巨头：称其有“马克思主义”倾向
sections.dek: 在交出亮眼财报后，Palantir CEO 亚历克斯·卡普却用“马克思主义”来形容 AI 行业，指责大模型公司试图“夺取生产资料”。
sections.body:
Palantir 刚刚发布了强劲的第二季度财报，营收增长惊人。但 CEO 亚历克斯·卡普在给股东的信中，却语出惊人，称 AI 行业有“马克思主义”的味道。他说，许多大语言模型公司，有意或无意地，试图“夺取他们所谓合作伙伴的生产资料”。

卡普的言下之意是，那些 AI 实验室，比如 OpenAI、Anthropic 等，可能通过提供模型，逐渐控制企业的核心数据和流程，让企业成为他们的附庸。而 Palantir 自己，则强调为客户提供定制化的 AI 解决方案，让客户掌握主动权。

这种论调，反映了 AI 产业链上不同角色的博弈。Palantir 作为应用层公司，担心被上游模型公司“卡脖子”；而模型公司则希望通过 API 和平台，扩大自己的影响力。

对于普通企业来说，选择 AI 供应商时，可能需要考虑“锁定”风险。如果过度依赖某家模型公司，未来可能失去议价能力。

从商业角度看，Palantir 的财报显示其 AI 业务增长迅猛，但卡普的言论也透露出对行业格局的担忧。他似乎在提醒客户，不要被模型公司的花言巧语所迷惑，要掌握自己的数据主权。

这种担忧并非空穴来风。随着 AI 模型越来越强大，企业可能越来越依赖它们，从而失去对自身业务的控制。Palantir 的定位是帮助企业构建自己的 AI 系统，而不是简单地调用外部 API。

对于普通用户来说，这场争论可能看似遥远，但实则关系到你使用的 AI 服务是否可靠、是否会被供应商绑架。未来，你可能需要更加关注 AI 服务的透明度和可移植性。

总的来说，Palantir 的指责揭示了 AI 产业链上“模型层”与“应用层”之间的紧张关系，企业选型时需警惕“被锁定”。

sections.body:
阿里巴巴今天发布了其最新的 AI 模型，并宣称其性能可以媲美 Anthropic 的 Claude。这已经不是阿里第一次向美国 AI 巨头发起挑战了。

从技术角度看，中国公司在大模型领域的发展，得益于庞大的数据资源和工程人才。尽管在高端芯片上受到限制，但通过算法优化和分布式训练，他们依然取得了显著进展。

对于产业来说，阿里的模型可能为开发者提供另一个选择，打破 OpenAI 等公司的垄断。对于普通用户，这意味着未来可能会有更多基于中国模型的 AI 应用出现。

从商业角度看，阿里发布新模型，不仅是技术上的竞争，更是市场策略的较量。阿里可能通过开源或低价策略，吸引更多开发者使用其模型，从而建立自己的生态系统。

这种竞争对全球 AI 市场是有益的。它迫使美国公司不断创新，同时也为全球开发者提供了更多选择。对于中国企业来说，这可能是突破美国技术封锁的一个机会。

总的来说，阿里新模型的发布，表明中美 AI 竞赛进入“贴身肉搏”阶段，中国公司正通过开源和性价比策略争夺市场。

sections.title: 苹果终于修复了 Siri，但为何让人感觉“不过如此”？
sections.dek: 苹果的 Siri AI 终于在测试版中上线，功能强大，但面对早已突飞猛进的 AI 助手，它的迟到让发布显得缺乏惊喜。
sections.body:
苹果终于推出了新版 Siri AI，在 iOS 27 的公测版中向所有用户开放。这款 Siri 经过了彻底改造，功能强大，能够完成多步骤任务，甚至能理解上下文。

然而，许多人的第一反应是：“就这？”因为苹果在 AI 上拖延了太久。在过去几年里，其他公司的 AI 助手已经能写代码、操作电脑、自主规划任务。相比之下，Siri 的“新能力”不过是追赶上了行业平均水平。

苹果的困境在于，它过于注重隐私保护，导致 AI 功能开发缓慢。而竞争对手则更激进，愿意用数据换取智能。

对于苹果用户来说，新版 Siri 确实更好用了，但可能不会让你惊艳。苹果需要在 AI 上拿出更激进的策略，否则在下一个时代可能掉队。

从技术角度看，Siri AI 的改进包括更自然的语言理解、更强的上下文记忆，以及与其他应用的深度集成。这些功能在技术上并不算超前，但苹果的整合能力使其体验更加流畅。

然而，AI 竞赛的节奏已经改变。如今，AI 助手不仅要能回答问题，还要能主动执行任务，甚至预测用户需求。苹果的 Siri 在这些方面还有很长的路要走。

对于开发者来说，Siri AI 的开放可能带来新的应用场景，但苹果的封闭生态也可能限制创新。相比之下，其他平台的 AI 助手更加开放，允许第三方开发者自由集成。

对于普通用户来说，Siri AI 的改进意味着你的 iPhone 将更智能，但你可能不会因此改变对苹果的看法。苹果需要证明自己不只是“追赶者”，而是能够引领 AI 创新的公司。

总的来说，苹果的 Siri AI 终于上线，但 AI 竞赛的节奏已经改变，苹果需要证明自己不只是“追赶者”。

根据最新数据，美国国会在 AI 工具上的支出，绝大部分都流向了 ChatGPT。这款由 OpenAI 开发的聊天机器人，已经成为议员和工作人员处理日常事务的得力助手，从起草文件到分析政策，无所不包。

这一现象反映了 AI 在政府领域的快速渗透。国会作为立法机构，也开始依赖 AI 来提高效率。但这也引发了担忧：如果立法者过度依赖某一家公司的 AI，是否会影响决策的客观性？

从商业角度看，OpenAI 在政府市场的成功，为其带来了稳定的收入来源，并可能影响未来的 AI 监管政策。毕竟，当监管者每天都在使用你的产品时，他们更可能制定对你有利的规则。

对于普通公民来说，这意味着 AI 正在影响公共政策，但公众对此的知情和参与还远远不够。

从技术角度看，ChatGPT 之所以能在国会普及，是因为其易用性和强大的文本处理能力。它可以帮助议员快速总结报告、起草演讲稿、分析法案影响等。这种效率提升是显而易见的。

然而，这也带来了数据安全和隐私问题。国会处理的信息往往涉及国家安全和敏感议题，如果这些数据被用于训练模型，可能会造成泄露风险。因此，OpenAI 可能需要为政府客户提供更高级别的数据保护。

此外，这种依赖也可能导致“技术垄断”。如果国会只使用 ChatGPT，那么其他 AI 公司将被排除在政府市场之外，这可能不利于竞争和创新。

对于普通用户来说，ChatGPT 在国会的普及，可能预示着 AI 将在更多公共领域发挥作用。但你也需要关注，这些 AI 系统是否透明、是否受到有效监管。

总的来说，ChatGPT 在美国国会的普及，展示了 AI 在政府领域的潜力，但也带来了“监管者被被监管者影响”的风险。

reading.synthesis: 今天的五条新闻，勾勒出 AI 产业的三条主线：一是监管的落地，欧洲率先为 AI 戴上“紧箍咒”；二是商业竞争的加剧，Palantir 与 AI 实验室的矛盾公开化，阿里则试图在模型能力上挑战美国；三是应用场景的拓展与尴尬，苹果的 Siri 姗姗来迟，而 ChatGPT 已经渗透进美国国会。这些事件共同表明，AI 的“上半场”拼的是模型能力，而“下半场”拼的是落地、合规与生态。

podcast.title: AI 监管、巨头与开源：今天的科技世界发生了什么？
podcast.description: 从欧盟 AI 透明度规则生效、Palantir CEO 的“马克思主义”言论，到阿里发布新模型、苹果 Siri AI 姗姗来迟，再到 ChatGPT 在国会的普及，今天的科技新闻勾勒出一幅 AI 产业走向成熟与博弈的图景。

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text: 你好，欢迎收听今天的伊恩每日·科技。我是伊恩。今天是2026年8月4日，科技世界发生了不少事。我们从一个具体的场景开始：如果你今天早上在欧洲打开手机，可能会看到一些新的AI标签——欧盟的AI透明度规则今天正式生效。这意味着，当你在网上和聊天机器人对话时，对方必须告诉你它是AI；当你看到一段深度伪造的视频时，它会被明确标记。而与此同时，大洋彼岸，一家美国AI公司的CEO却语出惊人，说AI行业有“马克思主义”色彩。这两件事看似无关，但都指向同一个问题：AI正在从技术竞赛变成社会规则的重塑。今天，我们就来聊聊这些变化。

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text:
今天，欧盟《人工智能法案》的第一批实质性规则正式生效了。从今天起，如果你在欧洲打开一个聊天机器人，或者刷到一段AI生成的深度伪造视频，平台必须明确告诉你：这是AI。这就像食品包装上的配料表，让AI的使用变得透明可见。

这项规则覆盖所有在欧盟运营的AI服务，不管公司总部在硅谷还是上海。具体来说，聊天机器人必须披露自己不是人类；深度伪造内容必须打上清晰标识。对普通人而言，这意味着当你和客服对话时，对方是AI还是真人，你会第一时间知道；当一段政客视频被AI换脸时，你也会被提醒。

这背后是欧盟一贯的思路：技术可以发展，但权利必须保护。去年《人工智能法案》通过后，这是第一批落地的条款，属于高风险AI监管的前奏。后续还有更严格的规则，比如对高风险AI系统的评估要求，会在未来几年逐步生效。

但批评的声音也不少。有分析指出，这些规则来得太晚，执行力度可能不足，更像是一种“象征性”的合规。比如，深度伪造的标识如何验证？平台会不会只是走个形式？这些疑问确实存在。不过，无论如何，这是全球首个全面的AI监管框架，它的实施，会让其他地区重新思考自己的监管策略。

对普通人来说，最直接的影响是：你在欧洲上网，会看到更多AI标识，这可能会让一些体验变得不那么流畅，但也会减少被AI欺骗的风险。对企业来说，合规成本增加了，尤其是那些依赖AI交互的科技公司。但长远看，透明的AI环境，或许能建立更深的用户信任。

欧盟的这一步，就像在高速公路上设置了第一个红绿灯。AI还在加速，但规则已经开始跟上。

blocks.speaker: listener
blocks.text: 伊恩，这些规则对普通用户有什么实际影响？我们真的会在意聊天对象是不是AI吗？

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text: 好问题。表面上看，你可能觉得无所谓，但想想看：当你接到一个推销电话，对方声音很自然，你以为是真人，结果发现是AI，你会不会有一种被欺骗的感觉？透明度规则就是保护你的知情权。它让你在知情的情况下做出选择，比如你可以决定是否继续对话。长期看，这会影响AI产品的设计——公司会倾向于让AI更透明，而不是伪装成人类。所以，它不只是标签，而是AI伦理落地的一个开始。

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text:
今天想跟你聊一家你可能不太熟悉，但在AI圈里非常特别的公司——Palantir。就在昨天，这家以大数据分析闻名的公司发布了第二季度财报，业绩好得惊人：美国商业收入同比增长149%，总营收增长93%。按理说，CEO应该兴高采烈地感谢AI时代，但他们的CEO亚历克斯·卡普却在股东信里语出惊人，说AI行业有“马克思主义”色彩。你没听错，就是那个马克思。

卡普的原话是：“我们的业务有马克思主义的弦外之音。”他指的是，那些构建大型语言模型的公司，比如OpenAI、Anthropic，他们“有意或无意地，意图夺取他们所谓合作伙伴的生产资料。”在卡普看来，这些AI实验室就像资本家，想控制客户的数据和流程，把客户变成依附于他们的“无产阶级”。

这个比喻很尖锐，但也很矛盾——Palantir的业绩恰恰是AI热潮带来的。那卡普到底在抱怨什么？其实，这反映的是AI产业链上的一场主导权之争。Palantir的商业模式，是为政府和大型企业提供定制化的数据分析服务，他们强调“人在回路”，也就是让客户自己掌控决策。而通用大模型公司，比如OpenAI，他们提供的是标准化的API，客户的数据要经过他们的服务器，模型也是他们训练的。卡普担心的是，如果企业习惯了直接用通用模型，那Palantir这种定制化服务还有价值吗？更关键的是，客户的数据和业务逻辑，会不会被模型提供商“锁死”？

卡普的批评，其实点出了AI产业的一个核心矛盾：模型提供商和下游应用公司之间，谁才是真正的主导者？Palantir的立场很明确：他们为客户提供“最后一公里”的定制化服务，让AI真正融入客户的业务，而不是让客户被通用模型绑住。卡普甚至说，Palantir是“反AI实验室的”，因为他们不卖模型，而是卖解决方案。

这场争论，对普通人有什么影响呢？你可能觉得，这是公司之间的商业竞争，跟我有什么关系？但你想，如果你是一家小企业的老板，你想用AI来优化你的供应链，你是直接用OpenAI的API，还是找Palantir这样的公司定制？前者便宜、快，但你的数据要交给别人；后者贵、慢，但你的数据更安全，系统也更贴合你的业务。这其实是一个“效率”和“控制权”的权衡。

卡普的“马克思主义”论，虽然听起来有点夸张，但他提醒了我们：在AI时代，谁掌握了数据和生产工具，谁就掌握了话语权。这不仅仅是商业问题，也是社会问题。未来，我们每个人都要面对类似的抉择：是拥抱大平台的便利，还是保护自己的数据主权？

好了，今天关于Palantir和卡普的争论就聊到这里。明天见。

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text: 今天，阿里又向美国的AI主导地位发起了一次冲击。据The Verge报道，阿里发布了一款新模型，声称其性能可以媲美Anthropic的Claude Fable 5。这并非阿里首次这样做，过去一年里，中国的大模型在性能上不断逼近美国，尤其在开源领域。阿里选择开源其模型，意味着任何人都可以免费使用、修改甚至商用，这大大降低了AI技术的门槛。对开发者而言，开源模型意味着你可以真正拥有模型，而不是被锁定在某个商业平台上，这无疑是一个极具吸引力的选择。也正是这种模式，让一些美国公司感到威胁——当中国模型在性能上不相上下，且完全开放时，美国公司依靠闭源和API收费的商业模式就可能受到冲击。这场中美AI竞赛，已经从单纯的技术比拼，扩展到了生态和商业模式的较量。对普通人来说，开源模型意味着更多选择，也意味着AI工具的成本可能进一步下降。但也要看到，开源模型的滥用风险同样存在，这需要监管和技术手段共同应对。

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text: 今天要聊的这件事，可能让你觉得有点熟悉：苹果的Siri AI终于来了，但感觉却有点平淡。先交代事实：在多次延迟之后，苹果在iOS 27的公测版中向所有用户开放了新的Siri AI。苹果兑现了之前的承诺，Siri变得更智能，能理解上下文，也能处理更复杂的请求。但为什么很多人觉得不过如此？因为AI世界已经变了。现在，AI能写代码、能执行多步骤任务，甚至能主动帮你操作电脑。相比之下，Siri AI只是让Siri变得“足够好”，而不是“领先”。苹果的迟到，让Siri失去了先发优势。不过，Siri AI有一个关键卖点：隐私和生态整合。它可以在你的设备上本地运行，处理个人信息，而不需要把数据上传到云端。这是苹果一贯的策略，也是它区别于其他AI的护城河。但问题在于，在AI竞赛中，慢一步可能意味着失去用户的注意力。苹果能否靠隐私和生态扳回一局，还有待观察。

blocks.speaker: listener
blocks.text: 苹果的Siri AI听起来还是很有苹果特色，那它到底值不值得用户期待？

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text: 值不值得，取决于你在乎什么。如果你在乎隐私，Siri AI是唯一的选择，因为它在设备端处理数据。如果你在乎功能，它可能不如那些云端AI强大，但日常使用足够。苹果的策略是让AI成为你生活的助手，而不是一个万能工具。所以，如果你是苹果生态的深度用户，Siri AI会让你觉得更方便；但如果你追求最前沿的AI能力，可能还是要看其他产品。

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text:
想象一下，美国国会的办公室里，议员和他们的助手们正在用ChatGPT起草文件、分析数据，甚至可能写演讲稿。这不是科幻场景，而是正在发生的事实。根据最新数据，联邦政府的AI工具采购中，ChatGPT占了90%。换句话说，当立法者一边讨论如何监管AI，一边却已经离不开它时，这个场景本身就充满了讽刺。

先看事实。TechCrunch报道，ChatGPT已经成为国会最受欢迎的AI工具。CNBC的数据显示，在联邦政府的AI采购中，ChatGPT占据了90%的份额。这意味着，从撰写备忘录到分析选民来信，ChatGPT已经深度嵌入立法工作的日常。

为什么是ChatGPT？原因并不复杂。它上手快，无需专门培训；它功能强大，能处理文本、数据，甚至生成初步的政策草案；它价格相对低廉，对于预算有限的政府机构来说，性价比很高。相比之下，其他AI工具要么门槛高，要么功能单一，难以满足议员们的多样化需求。

但问题也随之而来。当立法者依赖AI工具时，他们如何监管AI？这有点像让狐狸看管鸡窝。议员们用ChatGPT起草法案，而他们又要制定规则来约束这类AI工具。这种双重角色，难免让人担忧。

更具体地说，风险在哪里？首先是数据安全。议员们处理的信息往往涉及国家安全、选民隐私，如果这些数据被输入到ChatGPT中，会不会有泄露的风险？其次是偏见问题。AI模型基于训练数据，如果训练数据本身存在偏见，那么生成的文本也可能带有偏见，从而影响立法决策的公正性。

当然，我们也要看到积极的一面。AI确实能提高政府效率。比如，快速整理大量文件，辅助分析复杂数据，甚至帮助起草初稿，节省了时间和人力。但效率提升的同时，必须建立相应的监督机制。

对普通人来说，这意味着什么？当你的代表用AI来理解你的诉求时，你的声音可能会被算法简化或曲解。如果AI系统出现错误，谁来负责？这不仅是技术问题，更是治理问题。

所以，国会一边用着ChatGPT，一边讨论AI监管，这个场景虽然讽刺，但也提供了一个观察窗口：AI已经渗透到权力核心，而监管者本身也是使用者。这种“既当运动员又当裁判员”的局面，注定充满张力。未来，我们或许会看到更多关于AI透明度和责任归属的讨论，而这一切，都始于今天国会办公室里那一个个打开的ChatGPT窗口。

blocks.speaker: listener
blocks.text: 政府使用ChatGPT会不会有安全风险？比如机密信息泄露？

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text: 确实有风险。ChatGPT会把输入的数据发送到OpenAI的服务器，如果议员输入了敏感信息，就可能泄露。虽然OpenAI声称会保护数据，但政府机构通常有更高的安全标准。所以，我们看到一些机构开始限制使用，或者开发自己的内部AI工具。但问题是，如果政府不用ChatGPT，可能效率会降低。这是一个权衡。未来，我们可能会看到更多针对政府AI使用的专门规定。

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text: 今天的故事，其实都在讲同一件事：AI正在从技术竞赛变成社会规则的重塑。欧盟的监管，是在给AI套上缰绳；Palantir的争论，是产业内部的权力博弈；阿里的开源，是生态竞争；苹果的迟到，是产品策略的调整；国会的使用，是AI渗透到权力机构。这些事件交织在一起，告诉我们：AI不再是科幻，而是我们每天要面对的现实。它既是工具，也是挑战。作为普通人，我们需要理解这些变化，才能更好地适应未来。

blocks.speaker: ian
blocks.text: 好了，今天的伊恩每日·科技就到这里。我们聊了欧盟的AI监管、Palantir的争议、阿里的新模型、苹果的Siri AI，以及国会和ChatGPT。如果你对这些话题有什么想法，欢迎在评论区告诉我。明天见，我是伊恩，我们继续关注科技世界的每一个变化。
